Change self loathing into productive criticisim.

Self loathing is pointless but self reflection and being able to give yourself productive criticism is good.

For example:

I'm so chicken shit I never accomplish anything

compared to:

I know I get discouraged easily. What can I do to help me be less fearful?

The last line of thinking creates a path for improvement while the other insures you stay in a hole.

First remember that we are humans. We make mistakes. Have you learned from your mistakes? Then you have grown. If you haven't, then put some effort into getting some value from your mistakes. People tend to be harder on themselves then they are on other people. Think of it like that celebrity you love and think is awesome and perfect. They're not. In fact they're usually more fucked up than you. The difference is that you only see the highlight reel and not the outtakes. In your life you get all the highlights and all the outtakes.

When you find yourself wallowing in self-pity, find something to do. Break the cycle. Enrich yourself. Find something that makes you a better person. Maybe its working out, maybe it's learning something new, maybe it's just trying something new, like skydiving or zip lining.

We, as humans, are very good at beating ourselves up.

Lastly, remember this: If you cannot change it, how is worrying about it going to help? Accept it and move on.

"Well, I can't change that, but I can do "X" to make myself a better person"

I am / was pretty much like you. I started to lower my standards (which is = demands in my mind) to be less forgiving and more accepting of mistakes. Before, if I was not perfect, it was not good enough. If I made a mistake, it was the end and I had no worth that day.

Changing my standards / demands has actually caused me to be a much stronger and better person. Ironically I managed to raise the standard of my outcomes by lowering my standards. This way, you're not standing in your own way. And you'll be surprised how much energy you have inside you if you're not standing in your own way.

So how did you make that change?

First of all, it's not a binary white-black thing. It takes time and is a slow process. It started with me decreasing the importance of certain things. It seems counterintuitive at first, but that was the only way for me to ease up on the pressure and lord and behold, things went pretty much just as well as they did when I had the super amounts of pressure. When I realized that I could ease up on the pressure and get similar results, I in tandem discovered that I got so much more will / energy to do things, since I was no longer scared of the outcome. And once you get to that point, it's a snowballing effect.
